description:
Two Error variants carry only a fixed-string 'reason' as their payload (lib.rs:173-199):

    Error::ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> }
    Error::OcspDelegation   { reason: Cow<'static, str> }

The rustdoc on each field documents the design (lines 170-181, 190-198): the reason is a 'fixed-string description suitable for logging' and explicitly tells callers 'pattern-match on the variant rather than the inner string'. That documentation is honest about the constraint, but the constraint itself is the smell: programmatic callers get one bit of discriminator (which variant) for what is internally a many-way classification.

Today the producers in this PR write five distinct ProfileViolation reason strings:
  - 'TSA certificate has no ExtendedKeyUsage extension' (two arms, lib.rs:1427, 1433 — already flagged by PKIX-q9hv.15 area)
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage extension must be marked critical (RFC 3161 §2.3)'
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage extension is malformed'
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage must contain only id-kp-timeStamping (RFC 3161 §2.3)'
  - 'TSA KeyUsage extension is malformed'
  - 'TSA KeyUsage must contain only digitalSignature and/or nonRepudiation (...)'

A caller that wants to log 'TSA EKU not critical' counts vs. 'TSA EKU not sole' counts cannot do so without grepping the reason text — a notoriously fragile pattern across release boundaries.

Idiomatic Rust answer: replace the string field with a sub-enum.

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    #[non_exhaustive]
    pub enum ProfileViolationKind {
        TsaEkuExtensionMissing,
        TsaEkuNotCritical,
        TsaEkuMalformed,
        TsaEkuNotSoleTimestamping,
        TsaKeyUsageMalformed,
        TsaKeyUsageForbiddenBit, // could carry the offending bit
        // ... add more as wrappers grow
    }
    ProfileViolation(ProfileViolationKind)

Display can still produce the same fixed-string output via match. Callers gain programmatic dispatch; the workspace gains a place to attach structured data later (e.g. 'TsaKeyUsageForbiddenBit { bit: KeyUsageBit }') without churning the outer Error API. AGENTS.md §error-handling explicitly flags this anti-pattern: 'Error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields. Err(format!("expected {x}, got {y}")) loses the values; a structured variant keeps them accessible to callers who want to handle them.'

Adjacent but distinct from PKIX-q9hv.19 (non_exhaustive on the struct-variant shape). That fix freezes the variant shape; this fix changes the shape from string-typed to enum-typed. Both apply.

Cost of leaving it: forever-commitment to stringly-typed sub-classification. Pre-1.0 is the cheap time to fix. Post-1.0 the sub-enum becomes a breaking change.
title: Error::ProfileViolation / ::OcspDelegation stringly-typed reason field is non-idiomatic for a public error
